content: 1. Co-administration of levomilnacipran with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors, such as ritonavir, increases the levels of linagliptin by altering hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor the patient closely. 2. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of linagliptin by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor the patient closely. 3. Ritonavir decreases the effects of linagliptin through mechanisms other than CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor the patient closely. 4. Lopinavir decreases the effects of linagliptin through mechanisms other than CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor the patient closely. 5. Reports indicate that protease inhibitors, such as ritonavir and lopinavir, may cause hyperglycemia due to insulin resistance. Monitor blood glucose levels and adjust therapy as needed. 6. Ritonavir decreases the effects of liraglutide through mechanisms other than CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor the patient closely. 7. Lopinavir decreases the effects of liraglutide through mechanisms other than CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor the patient closely. 8. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of lofepramine by affecting hepatic CYP2D6 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor the patient closely. 9. Both lopinavir and lofexidine increase the QTc interval. Exercise caution, monitor the patient closely, and consider ECG monitoring. 10. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of lofexidine by affecting hepatic CYP2D6 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor the patient closely. 11. Concomitant use of lofexidine with strong CYP2D6 inhibitors may increase plasma levels of lofexidine. Monitor for symptoms of orthostasis and bradycardia, and consider reducing the dose of lofexidine. 12. Lomitapide increases the levels of ritonavir by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Modify therapy and monitor the patient closely. Consider reducing the dose of ritonavir when used concomitantly with lomitapide. 13. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of loperamide by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Exercise caution and monitor the patient closely. 14. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of lopinavir by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor the patient closely. 15. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of loratadine by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Loratadine also increases the levels or effects of ritonavir by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Exercise caution and monitor the patient closely. 16. Lorcaserin increases the levels or effects of ritonavir by affecting hepatic CYP2D6 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor the patient closely. 17. Lorlatinib decreases the levels or effects of lopinavir by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor the patient closely. 18. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of losartan by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor the patient closely. 19. Ritonavir increases the levels of lumacaftor/ivacaftor by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor the patient closely. A threefold increase in exposure may occur. 20. Due to the induction effect of lumacaftor on CYP3A, the net exposure of ivacaftor at steady state is not expected to exceed that of ivacaftor monotherapy at the approved dose of 150 mg every 12 hours. No dose adjustment is necessary when CYP3A inhibitors are initiated in patients already taking lumacaftor/ivacaftor. 21. When initiating lumacaftor/ivacaftor in patients taking strong CYP3A inhibitors, reduce the dose to one tablet daily (lumacaftor 200 mg/ivacaftor 125 mg total daily dose) for the first week to allow for the steady-state induction effect of lumacaftor. After this period, continue with the recommended daily dose. 22. No dose adjustment is required for moderate or weak CYP3A4 inhibitors. 23. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of lumateperone by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor the patient closely. 24. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of lumateperone by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor the patient closely. 25. When co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors, reduce the dose of lumateperone to 5 mg/day. Monitor the patient closely. 26. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of lumefantrine by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor the patient closely. 27. Lumefantrine decreases the levels or effects of lopinavir by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor the patient closely. 28. Lopinavir may either increase or decrease the levels of lumefantrine. Monitor the patient closely. 29. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of maraviroc by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Decrease the dose of maraviroc to 150 mg twice daily when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Monitor for potential increased toxicity. 30. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of marijuana by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Marijuana also increases the levels or effects of ritonavir and lopinavir by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor the patient closely. 31. Mavorixafor increases the levels or effects of ritonavir by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Exercise caution and monitor the patient closely. 32. Both mavorixafor and lopinavir increase the QTc interval. Modify therapy, monitor the patient closely, and consider ECG monitoring. 33. Mavorixafor causes concentration-dependent QTc prolongation. Monitor QTc during treatment in patients with risk factors for QTc prolongation, such as co-administered medications that increase mavorixafor exposure or other drugs with a high risk of QTc prolongation. 34. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of mavorixafor by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Modify therapy and monitor the patient closely. 35. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of mavorixafor by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor the patient closely. 36. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of medroxyprogesterone by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor the patient closely. 37. Ritonavir increases the levels of meperidine by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor the patient closely for potential increased toxicity. 38. Lopinavir increases the levels of meperidine by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor the patient closely for potential increased toxicity. 39. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of mestranol by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism and inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. However, ritonavir may also decrease mestranol levels by increasing its metabolism. This may result in contraceptive failure; use additional or alternative contraceptive methods. 40. Ritonavir decreases the effects of metformin through mechanisms other than CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor the patient closely.
